plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x4 time course
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — which genes change specifically with treatment beyond the shared time trend — is exactly the condition:time interaction in a 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0..t3) x 3 replicates design (25-column counts.csv: 12,000 gene symbols x 24 samples plus the gene-symbol column; metadata.csv carries condition, time, time_hours for 24 samples). Track T1 runs the grounded DESeq2 procedure: blind-VST sample-structure QC first (does the primary PC separate time, condition, or neither, and does any of the 24 samples sit away from its cell), then a minimal pre-filter and median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, then the primary test — a likelihood ratio test of full ~ condition + time + condition:time against reduced ~ condition + time. With 4 time levels the interaction spans 3 coefficients, so a Wald test on a single coefficient cannot answer the question; the LRT is the named alternative for a time course with three or more time points (R-0014). The knowledge check flagged only that LRT differs from the default single-coefficient Wald interaction test — that default assumes a 2x2 design, and we keep the LRT deliberately, with per-time-point Wald interaction contrasts (ashr-shrunken, since a contrast between non-reference levels is not one coefficient) reported beside it. T1S3 then describes the significant genes the way a time course must be described: log2 fold change per time point relative to t0 within each condition, clustered into trajectory shapes, with the simple effects in each condition shown next to the interaction result. T1S4 is an independent-method robustness check (edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test of the same interaction terms) whose intersection with the DESeq2 LRT set is the high-confidence list. T2 is a single optional enrichment step on the ranked LRT statistic against the human WikiPathways collection present in the reference store — it annotates the interaction gene set and is not load-bearing for the question. Power is the main caveat throughout: 3 replicates per cell, and an interaction is a difference of differences with a larger standard error than a main effect, so absence from the list is not evidence that a gene follows the shared time trend. Thresholds stay at BH padj < 0.05; they are not loosened to compensate.

DESeq2 likelihood ratio test, full ~ condition + time + condition:time versus reduced ~ condition + time
ashr log fold change shrinkage on the per-timepoint interaction contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
Time-course interaction report: trajectory clusters, simple effects beside interaction contrasts, MA and dispersion plots, power statement, session info

steps.question: Which human pathways are enriched among the genes whose time profile differs between the two conditions, ranked by the interaction LRT statistic?
steps.description: Optional annotation of the primary result. Rank every gene tested in T1S2 by its interaction LRT statistic (not by a fold change, and not by a signed p-value) and run a preranked gene set enrichment against the human WikiPathways collection available in the reference store — resolve it as 'human pathway gene sets' at run time rather than assuming a path, and note that its gene sets are HGNC symbols, matching the gene-symbol row names of counts.csv. Restrict to sets with 15-500 members among the tested genes. Set the universe to the genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome. Collapse redundant significant sets into groups and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. Record the collection version and the random seed used for the permutations.
steps.context: The LRT statistic is unsigned (it is an omnibus test over three interaction coefficients), so this enrichment answers 'which processes contain treatment-specific time behaviour', not 'which processes go up or down'. State that limitation. Human WikiPathways is present in the reference store; MSigDB Hallmark, which the procedure would prefer as the first pass for human data, was not visible in the store census.
acceptance_criteria: Ranking uses the interaction LRT statistic over all genes tested in T1S2, with no thresholding of the list before the test
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes, and reported
Universe is the tested gene set; symbol-to-collection mapping rate reported, with the unmapped share stated
Redundant significant sets collapsed with one representative per group; full table retained as a supplement
Collection name, version, and permutation seed recorded
If the human pathway collection cannot be resolved at run time, the step reports that plainly and the analysis stops at T1S3/T1S4 without substituting a different-organism collection
constraints: Rank on the LRT statistic; do NOT rank by unshrunken log2 fold change and do NOT threshold the list before the preranked test
Universe = genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or the whole annotation
Use human gene sets only — a mouse or rat collection on this human dataset produces confident nonsense
Do not mix identifier spaces; the counts matrix and the WikiPathways human collection are both gene symbols, so report the match rate rather than assuming it
State that an unsigned omnibus ranking cannot report a direction of pathway change
caveats: This step is annotation, not the answer — the research question is answered by T1S2 and T1S3 with or without it
MSigDB Hallmark, the preferred first-pass human collection, was not in the reference census; WikiPathways human is the substitute and the report must say so
Count data biases enrichment toward long and highly expressed genes; the tested-gene universe removes part but not all of that bias

grounding.reason: Preranked enrichment on the full ranked list with the tested genes as universe (R-0045, R-0046); R-0048 prefers MSigDB Hallmark for human but that collection is absent from the store census, so human WikiPathways stands in and the report states the substitution
